{{Quote|Ah, these pit droids. You gotta tell 'em what to do every minute!|[[Watto/Legends|Watto]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Pit Droids">''[[Star Wars: Pit Droids]]''</ref>}}
A '''DUM-series pit droid''', or simply called a '''pit droid''', was a [[Droid/Legends|droid]] manufactured by [[Serv-O-Droid, Inc./Legends|Serv-O-Droid, Inc.]] and constructed in large quantities on [[Cyrillia/Legends|Cyrillia]] by the native [[Cyrillian]]s for use in labor, repair and light construction. They were also associated with repairing [[Podracer/Legends|podracers]] at [[Podracing/Legends|podracing]] events.<ref name="SWE pit droid" />

==Characteristics==
[[File:PitDroids-WiaW05.png|thumb|left|180px|A pair of pit droids hard at work, demonstrating their immense strength.]]
Pit droids stood at a relatively diminutive 1.19 meters tall and came in many different colors. Their most remarkable feature was their immense strength, able to carry objects many times their own size or weight. This enabled them to repair automata such as [[Podracer/Legends|Podracers]] at a remarkable pace. Their skeletal design and long, thin limbs were dwarfed by their broad-flared, dome-shaped heads. In the center of their head was a large, round [[Photoreceptor/Legends|photoreceptor]] equipped with multi-spectrum scanners. The photoreceptor could detect microscopic damage in metals and other solids.<ref name="EV" />

The DUM-series worked best in large groups, and had built-in comm systems that allowed them to communicate with those in their unit. The antennas on their disk-shaped heads served to transmit directions to other droids, allowing a group of droids to collaborate on a project more efficiently and thereby expediting its completion.<ref name="EV" /> Their immense strength would make a malfunctioning (or unattended) unit extremely hazardous, possibly resulting in significant damage. The most hazardous of these was a damaged ON/OFF button, the risk of which caused many owners to keep [[Ion cannon/Legends|ion]] [[Blaster/Legends|blaster]] on hand as a precautionary measure. If a unit was past the brink of repair they would need to be disposed of, almost always resulting in the disintegration of the unfortunate droid.

Pit droids could compress themselves into a compact, box-shaped package. A tap on their photorecepter would signal them to return to their upright position, and vice-versa. There were also [[launcher]]s specifically made to automatically decompress and release individual pit droids, one at a time.<ref name="Star Wars: Pit Droids" />

==History==
Mass-produced by [[Serv-O-Droid, Inc./Legends|Serv-O-Droid, Inc.]] in factories on [[Cyrillia/Legends|Cyrillia]], the DUM-series droids were commonly used in garages across [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] during the days of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. In production for several decades, the DUM-series garnered criticism in the press due to their reputation as poorly programmed. Clumsy and hapless, the droids were cheaply made and often were recycled rather than repaired. Despite the criticism, the DUM-series droids were capable within their narrow range of abilities.<ref name="EV" />

While being much maligned in the press, the droids were popular in the Outer Rim, even during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]].<ref name="EV" /> They had seen much use on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] in [[Wald's Parts|Watto's Shop]] and at the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] working on [[Podracer/Legends|podracers]], though a handful were also purchased by [[Aneesa Dym]] to make repairs to her ship, the ''[[Dusty Duck]]''. When [[Jar Jar Binks/Legends|Jar Jar Binks]] visited Watto's Shop in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], he accidentally activated a dormant pit droid, although he quickly turned it off when [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]] instructed him to hit it in the nose.

During the Boonta Eve Classic of 32 BBY while the racer [[Ody Mandrell/Legends|Ody Mandrell]] had his pod in a pit-stop, a single DUM-series pit droid was sucked into the engine and thrown out the opposite end of the engine. The droid "survived," (even letting out a cheer of excitement) but Ody's engine did not, costing him the race. Pit droids would also be used to scavenge any reusable rubble from podracers that had blown apart. This action could be quite hazardous, as the droids were likely to be destroyed by functional podracers that were still running the course; however, the low cost of an individual unit made the loss of a single droid worth the risk.

In [[22 BBY/Legends|22 BBY]], the first year of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]], several pit droids assisted [[Corporate Alliance/Legends|Corporate Alliance]] [[Magistrate/Legends|Magistrate]] [[Passel Argente/Legends|Passel Argente]] on unloading much of the Magistrate's treasure in [[Lessu City/Legends|Lessu]], the [[Capital/Legends|capital]] [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Ryloth/Legends|Ryloth]].<ref name="Covetous" /> Another pit droid, [[WAC-47/Legends|WAC-47]], was assigned to [[D-Squad/Legends|D-Squad]], after serving [[Clone Marshal Commander/Legends|Commander]] [[Neyo/Legends|Neyo]] of the [[91st Mobile Reconnaissance Corps/Legends|91st Mobile Reconnaissance Corps]], which was formed to steal a [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] [[Encryption module/Legends|encryption module]] during a [[Mission to steal a Separatist encryption module/Legends|mission]].<ref name="SW" />

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Pitdroidstack_wsmi.jpg|thumb|right|150px|Two highly incompetent pit droids.]]
In the game ''[[Star Wars: Pit Droids]]'' (Lucas Learning Games), the droids have various equipment: ladders, wrenches, cases, gas tanks, or nothing. They also have different colored heads and bodies.

In ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'', DUM-series pit droids are featured as playable characters, although they are incapable of doing anything useful. This is likely because the character was only added for novelty purposes.

According to the DVD commentary in [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], a scene that showed a squabble between three pit droids was a homage to ''The Three Stooges''.
